concepts.title: What is a Language Model
keyPoints: A probability distribution over token sequences, factored via chain rule into ∏ P(xᵢ|x_<i)
Pretraining minimizes cross-entropy between predicted and actual next token
Transformer decoder produces each conditional via causal (masked) self-attention
One model, two uses: score a sequence (perplexity) or generate (autoregressive sampling)
Optimized for plausible text, not truth — hallucination is structural, not a bug

concepts.title: Tokenization
keyPoints: Converts raw text into integer IDs from a fixed vocabulary
Subword schemes (BPE/WordPiece/Unigram) avoid word-level OOV and char-level bloat
BPE: iteratively merge the most frequent adjacent symbol pair
Common words become 1 token; rare words split into subwords
Permanent design choice; explains weak arithmetic, letter-counting, multilingual cost skew

concepts.title: Byte-Pair Encoding
keyPoints: Subword tokenization: starts from chars/bytes, merges frequent adjacent pairs
Training: count all adjacent-symbol pairs, merge most frequent, repeat to target vocab size
Ships two artifacts: vocab + an ordered merge-rule list
Encoding replays merges in learned order (lowest rank first), never recomputes frequencies
Gotcha: re-deriving frequency at encode time (not replaying trained order) silently breaks tokenization

concepts.title: Token Embeddings
keyPoints: Embedding matrix E ∈ ℝ^(V×d): one row per vocab token
Lookup is E[token_id] — pure indexing, not computation
Row geometry starts as noise; meaning emerges from next-token gradient descent
Rarely-seen tokens stay near random init → 'glitch tokens' (e.g. SolidGoldMagikarp)
Embedding table dominates params at small scale, negligible at large scale

concepts.title: Transformer Overview
keyPoints: Self-attention + feed-forward stack, no recurrence — trains fully in parallel
Each token computes Q/K/V; attends to all tokens via softmax(qk/√dk)
Attention is permutation-invariant — position injected via explicit embeddings (sinusoidal/learned)
Multi-head attention + residual/layer-norm: specialized heads, stable deep stacking
Gotcha: unscaled dot products saturate softmax — always scale by √dk

concepts.title: Encoder vs Decoder
keyPoints: Only structural diff: self-attention mask — bidirectional (encoder) vs causal (decoder)
Encoder: every position attends to all positions → good at understanding (BERT, embeddings)
Decoder: position i attends only to ≤i → matches train/inference for generation (GPT)
Encoder-decoder (T5): bidirectional encoder + causal decoder, linked via cross-attention
Gotcha: missing causal mask lets model peek at future token — loss looks great, generation is incoherent

concepts.title: Feed-Forward Network
keyPoints: Two-layer MLP applied independently to each token position
FFN(x) = W2·σ(W1x + b1) + b2, d_ff usually 4×d_model
σ is ReLU (original), GELU (BERT/GPT), or SwiGLU (LLaMA)
~2/3 of a block's params — target for quantization and MoE routing
Gotcha: no cross-token mixing — that's attention's job, not FFN's

concepts.title: Logits and the LM Head
keyPoints: Logit = raw unnormalized score per vocab token, pre-softmax
LM head: linear layer, logits = h @ W^T, shape (vocab_size, d_model)
Weight tying: LM head reuses input embedding matrix, saves ~524M params
Training needs logits at every position; generation needs only the last
Gotcha: slice hidden_states[:, -1:, :] before lm_head, not after

concepts.title: Positional Encodings
keyPoints: Self-attention is permutation-equivariant — position must be injected explicitly
Absolute: sinusoidal (fixed, trig-based) or learned table, added to input embeddings
Relative: ALiBi penalizes attention scores by distance; RoPE rotates Q/K vectors
RoPE's dot product depends only on relative offset (m−n), not absolute position
Gotcha: learned absolute hard-fails past max length; RoPE/sinusoidal silently degrade instead

concepts.title: Pretraining
keyPoints: Self-supervised next-token prediction over trillions of raw tokens
Loss = mean cross-entropy of -log P(x_t | x_<t)
Teacher forcing + causal mask: parallel training, sequential inference
Produces a fluent base model, not instruction-following or safe
Falling loss ≠ better assistant — that needs SFT/RLHF

concepts.title: Residual and Layer Norm
keyPoints: Residual: y = x + Sublayer(x), not y = F(x)
Identity term (I + dF/dx) stops gradients vanishing across depth
LayerNorm: per-token, over features — zero mean/unit variance × gain + bias
Batch-independent (unlike BatchNorm) — works at batch-size-1, variable-length decoding
Pre-norm (x + Sublayer(LN(x))) keeps residual stream clean; needs final ln_f

concepts.title: Self-Attention
keyPoints: Weighted average of Value vectors; weights = softmax(QK^T/√d_k)
Q, K, V = three projections of X; Q·K searches, V is content
Scale by √d_k — else large d_k saturates softmax, kills gradients
O(1) path length between any two tokens (vs O(n) for RNNs)
Permutation-invariant alone — needs positional encodings; O(n²) cost is mainly memory

concepts.title: Context Window
keyPoints: Max tokens (prompt + output) attended to in one forward pass
Absolute embeddings hard-cap length; RoPE/ALiBi generalize but degrade past training range
Attention is O(n²); KV cache grows linearly, often dominates GPU memory
Lost in the middle: mid-context info recalled less reliably than edges
Validate long-context claims with needle-in-a-haystack evals, not spec sheets

concepts.title: Multi-Head Attention
keyPoints: Runs h scaled dot-product attentions in parallel on learned Q/K/V projections
Split d_model into h heads of size d_k = d_model/h, softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V per head
Concatenate per-head outputs, mix back with final projection W_O
Same FLOPs/params as single-head — splitting heads is free, not 'spend more get more'
Reshape bug: use view+transpose not bare reshape, or heads silently scramble (no crash)

concepts.title: Quadratic Attention Cost
keyPoints: O(n²) compute & memory: every token's query scores every key
Builds S=QKᵀ (n×n matrix), softmax, then multiplies by V — O(n²·d)
Projections/MLP scale O(n·d²), linear — attention overtakes them past n≈2·d_model
FlashAttention: same O(n²) FLOPs, just cuts memory O(n²)→O(n); not linear attention
KV-cache makes each step O(n), but full generation is still O(n²) total

concepts.title: Quantization and QLoRA
keyPoints: Quantization: store weights in fewer bits (INT8/INT4/NF4) to cut memory/compute
q = round(W/scale), scale = max|W|/(2^(b-1)-1); error bounded by scale/2
QLoRA: freeze 4-bit NF4 base, train only bf16 LoRA adapters on top
No gradient touches quantized weights — sidesteps QAT's straight-through estimator
Blockwise (64-val) + double quantization avoids outlier-feature blowup at 6-7B+ scale

concepts.title: RLHF and Instruction Tuning
keyPoints: SFT: imitate curated (instruction, response) pairs via cross-entropy
RLHF: train reward model on human pairwise comparisons (Bradley-Terry)
Optimize SFT policy vs. reward model with PPO + KL penalty to SFT
Reward hacking: policy exploits reward-model blind spots (Goodhart's law)
DPO: closed-form alternative, skips the unstable RL loop

concepts.title: Sampling and Decoding
keyPoints: Decoding = turning per-step logits into a chosen token, autoregressively
Deterministic: greedy (argmax) or beam search (top-B by cumulative log-prob) maximize sequence likelihood
Stochastic: sample from softmax(logits/T), truncated via top-k, top-p, or min-p
Gotcha: max-likelihood text degenerates into repetition loops (Holtzman et al.), so sampling beats greedy for open-ended text
Correct order: temperature → softmax → top-k → top-p → renormalize → sample

concepts.title: Scaling Laws
keyPoints: Power-law relating pretraining loss to params (N), tokens (D), compute (C)
L(N,D) = E + A/N^α + B/D^β — irreducible entropy + capacity error + data error
Fit curve on small cheap runs, extrapolate to predict huge runs
Chinchilla: optimal is N and D scaling equally, ~20 tokens/param (not Kaplan's N≫D)
Gotcha: Chinchilla-optimal ignores inference cost — over-train smaller models for high-volume serving (LLaMA)

concepts.title: Hallucination
keyPoints: Next-token prediction optimizes plausible text, not verified truth
Intrinsic (contradicts input) vs extrinsic (unsupported addition) hallucination
Occurs in open-domain (parametric) and closed-domain (RAG) settings alike
RLHF worsens it — raters prefer confident answers over hedging
RAG bounds extrinsic but not intrinsic hallucination — still need verification

concepts.title: LoRA and Fine-Tuning
keyPoints: Freezes pretrained W; trains low-rank update ΔW = B·A instead
Works because task-specific weight updates have low intrinsic rank (r≪d) — e.g. r=8 gives 256× fewer trainable params
Forward pass: h = Wx + (alpha/r)·(B·A)·x; only B,A get gradients, W never moves
B initialized to zero (A small random) → ΔW=0 at step 0, training starts exactly at pretrained behavior
Frozen base still needs full GPU memory — QLoRA (4-bit quantized base) needed to fine-tune huge models on one GPU

concepts.title: Prefill vs Decode
keyPoints: Prefill: one parallel forward pass over all prompt tokens, builds KV cache
Decode: sequential loop, one token at a time, reads/extends KV cache
Prefill is compute-bound (matmul, high arithmetic intensity) → sets TTFT
Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound (matrix-vector, weights reused for 1 token) → sets TPOT
Fix decode's low intensity via batching (continuous batching); chunked prefill avoids head-of-line blocking

concepts.title: RAG vs Fine-Tuning
keyPoints: Two levers to adapt a frozen LLM: change the context (RAG) vs change the weights (fine-tuning)
RAG: embed query → nearest-neighbor search → splice top-k chunks into prompt (open-book)
Fine-tuning: extra gradient steps on (input, output) examples so behavior becomes the default (closed-book)
Use RAG for facts that are large/volatile/must-cite; fine-tune for tone, schema, tool-call conventions
Gotcha: fine-tuning on facts teaches imitation not knowledge — frozen, poorly generalized, harder-to-catch hallucinations

concepts.title: KV Cache
keyPoints: Caches per-layer K/V projections so decode reuses them instead of recomputing
Works because causal masking makes a token's K/V depend only on itself + earlier tokens
Prefill computes K/V for the whole prompt in parallel; decode appends one token's K/V per step
Size = 2 × layers × kv_heads × head_dim × seq_len × batch_size × bytes — often the real GPU-memory bottleneck
Doesn't cut attention's O(n²) cost, only removes redundant re-projection of past tokens

concepts.title: KV Cache Memory
keyPoints: GPU memory holding cached K/V tensors for every past token
Per token: 2 × n_kv_heads × head_dim × dtype_bytes, × layers
Scales linearly with seq_len & batch_size — can dwarf model weights
Decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound: reads the whole cache every step
Shrunk via GQA/MQA, INT8/FP8 quantization, PagedAttention, sliding-window eviction

concepts.title: KV Cache Eviction
keyPoints: Reclaims GPU memory by discarding cached K/V pairs for chosen tokens/sequences
Token-level: sliding window, StreamingLLM (window + attention-sink tokens), H2O (recent + heavy-hitters by cumulative attention)
Request-level: scheduler preempts whole sequences — swap to CPU or recompute via re-prefill
Fails silently — evicted context is just gone, no error, breaks long-context recall tasks
Different lever than quantization (fewer bytes/token) or prefix caching (reuse, not deletion)

concepts.title: KV Cache Tricks
keyPoints: Shrinks/bounds KV cache's memory and HBM-bandwidth cost during decoding
GQA/MQA: fewer KV heads than query heads — biggest lever (~8x cut)
Quantize cached K/V to int8/fp8 for cheap, retrain-free savings
PagedAttention: block-based cache + copy-on-write sharing of shared prefixes
Sliding-window/attention-sink bounds cache to O(1) — test long-context recall before shipping

concepts.title: MQA and GQA
keyPoints: Query heads share fewer K/V heads to shrink the KV cache
MQA: all query heads share a single K/V head (max compression)
GQA: query heads split into g groups, each sharing one K/V head
Dial g: g=1 recovers MQA, g=h recovers MHA; Llama2/3, Mistral use g=8
Gotcha: saves KV-cache bandwidth only — QK^T/softmax·V FLOPs barely change
